text:
devon: Heads up — canary running NCCL 3.5.2 on A100 pools is showing intermittent p2p queue-depth stalls. tail latency spikes ~3x on 99th for multi-GPU inference.

maria: ugh, saw that in the dashboard. any quick repro or logs?

devon: attaching excerpt from the canary job logs, truncated: 
```
[nccl] socket send failed: Resource temporarily unavailable
[nccl] enqueue timeout after 200ms, queue_depth=64
TRACE: collective allreduce timed out, retries=3
```

ashok: queue_depth=64 is our default for the runtime. 3.5.2 seems to hit backpressure more often vs 3.4.x. could be handshake pacing changes.

lina: can we try lowering queue depth + enable adaptive backoff? there are two knobs: `p2p.queue_depth` and `collective.backoff_ms`. small change first (queue_depth -> 48) to measure throughput/latency tradeoff.

devon: quick experiment: lowered to 48 in a canary, tail latency dropped ~30% but throughput lost ~8% on that microbench. still saw occasional enqueue timeout.

maria: 8% throughput loss is acceptable temporarily if it stabilizes latency for customer SLAs. what about increasing backoff jitter?

ashok: propose patch to runtime config: 
```yaml
p2p:
  queue_depth: 48
  adaptive_backoff: true
  backoff_ms: 50
  max_backoff_ms: 1000
collective:
  retry_limit: 5
  handshake_timeout_ms: 5000
```
This enables exponential backoff with jitter. should reduce hot socket retries.

devon: sounds good. need to test memory/KV cache impact too. also observed some kernel-level EAGAINs in dmesg on one node. may be driver/CUDA interplay.

lina: we should gate this behind canary + perf regression harness. add canary rule: fail if 99th latency increases >10% or throughput drop >12% vs baseline.

infra-bot: canary created: runtime-nccl-adaptive-backoff-2399994321. 50 pods in us-west1-a.

maria: if canary passes, we need rollout plan for Dedicated pools. suggest staged rollout by region with a 1-hour ramp and automatic rollback on error budget breach.

ashok: note on cost: lowering queue_depth and adding backoff increases CPU/latency overhead; will raise per-token marginal cost slightly for hosted. include cost note in release.

devon: one more experiment: on a smaller mixed-arch pool (A100 + H100) the stalls are worse. likely p2p parity issues. recommend we avoid mixed-arch for now while we evaluate NCCL 3.5.x.

lina: ack — add policy to smart-routing: prefer homogeneous pools for multi-GPU inference until we validate.

maria: action items:
- ashok: land config change behind feature flag + perf tests (ETA 4h)
- devon: run mixed-arch canary and collect kernel logs (ETA 2h)
- lina: update rollout playbook and smart-routing policy (ETA 6h)

devon: starting kernel log collection now. will paste compressed dmesg snippets if I see EAGAIN from nvlink. :mag:

infra-bot: canary update: 10/50 pods reporting enqueue timeouts, 40/50 stable. collecting traces.

maria: thanks. if the canary keeps these numbers we'll sign off on the adaptive backoff config and schedule a region-by-region rollout with a rollback on error budget triggers. :thumbsup:

devon: one last note — keep NCCL rollback path validated (3.4.x pinned image); raising a small runbook to avoid surprises during TTL windows.

ashok: added runbook PR: `docs/rollouts/nccl-3.5-backoff.md` with rollback commands and commands to force pinned image: 
```bash
kubectl set image ds/inference-runtime inference=redwood/runtime:nccl-3.4.9-pinned -n inference
kubectl rollout restart ds/inference-runtime -n inference
```

lina: cool. will schedule post-mortem if we need rollback.

maria: fine-grained testing next 8h. keep updates in this thread.

devon: will update with kernel log snippets and perf dashboards.

(ends)
